summaries.Good news: Researchers are turning science toward protecting nature and people—from identifying bee-safe pesticide repellents to archaeologists risking their lives saving cultural treasures, and workers finally getting fair compensation after years of exploitation.
summaries.Ideas: Information design is becoming a cultural statement, while practical guides help us reclaim focus and make smarter choices about the tools we use daily.
summaries.Technology: From wearable textiles that generate electricity to FDA-cleared exoskeletons giving spinal-cord patients independence, and AI-powered musical instruments opening new creative possibilities, technology is solving real human challenges.
summaries.Design: Design thinking is reshaping how we live—from radical space efficiency in capsule hotels and micro-homes to sustainable material innovation, and thoughtful reorientation of everyday objects like pens and tweezers that remove friction from creative work.

items.title: CA Researchers Identify Odors That Repel Honeybees From Pesticides
items.snippet: In a win for pollinator conservation, researchers at the University of California, Riverside, have identified chemical compounds that can safely repel honey bees from pesticide-treated crops. The research offers a potential solution to one of agriculture’s most urgent challenges: pesticides leading
items.line: Protecting honeybees while safeguarding crops represents a genuine breakthrough in balancing agriculture with pollinator survival.

items.title: Tent-like micro home unfolds into an off-grid A-frame
items.snippet: US design studio Atelier Lune has been awarded a 2026 Red Dot Design Award for a tent-like micro-home concept that is designed to be transported by car and set up quickly upon arrival. items.line: Camping House's foldable off-grid design reimagines lightweight living as a practical, elegant alternative to traditional construction.
